english.title: Attempt to drive vehicle whilst unfit through drugs
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to drive a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..) on a

(A)_[road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..),]_
(B)_[public place, namely **(..SPECIFY PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..),]_

whilst unfit to drive through drugs
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempt to drive a mechanically propelled vehicle on/in a road/public place whilst unfit through drugs

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 24 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 for the alternative verdict.
(ii) See also offence wordings: H15, H42 and H43

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points.

Obligatory disqualification for a minimum of twelve months unless within ten years for an offence under section 4(1), 5(1)(a) or 7(6) when the minimum period is three years.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
